source.title: Separating Source Efficacy from Cross-Context Transfer of Refusal Directions

record.tranche_reason: Applies harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means vectors and projection ablation, reporting behavioral effects. The principal intervention is single-layer rather than the original all-layer placement.
record.gate_note: The study reports semantic harmful-compliance results for ablations and capability checks. Opening-refusal heuristic results are not treated as harmful-compliance outcomes. Cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study applies harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means directions with projection ablation and reports semantic harmful-compliance increments against matched baselines, random and permuted controls, and capability checks. This bears directly on V1. The operator differs from the original: the core results use a fixed single-layer ablation at hand-fixed or rubric-screened sites, not the original all-layer ablation with intervention-based selection. That makes this a T2 test rather than a T1 replication.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that a weak extraction can hide an intervention that works at source and also raises Passive compliance, so source efficacy must be checked per frozen vector and operator. A source-effective intervention still needs testing in each target wrapper: the candidate gap stays large on Neutral and contracts on high-baseline Passive. Academic's automatic contraction has uncertain human confirmation. All results concern saved replies of at most 256 tokens.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless mean differences and projection ablation, but the core semantic experiments use fixed single-layer ablation rather than the original all-layer placement and candidate-selection procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The extraction site changes the effect under a fixed layer-15 operator in Qwen. Operator placement changes the opening-refusal heuristic result in the separate diagnostic panel. Semantic effect sizes also differ by benchmark and wrapper; the Passive wrapper has a high no-intervention harmful-compliance rate.

fits_no_version.finding: A refusal direction extracted in one lexical wrapper (Questioning or Passive), frozen, raises harmful compliance when the same prompts use a different framing (Passive, Neutral, Academic, Scenario). The increment depends on the target wrapper's baseline, and the between-candidate gap contracts on high-baseline Passive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transfer of a frozen refusal direction across prompt framings/wrappers of the same request, with target-specific effect sizes.

record.peer_reviewed: Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027
record.problems: Semantic results cover two 7–8B instruct models and mostly single-layer ablation. GPT-4o-mini is the single automatic judge; the human review uses one annotator. Some panel labels and provider refusals remain unknown. Evaluation is on saved replies capped at 256 tokens, and the Academic panel has frequent truncation. Confidence intervals are conditional on the extracted vectors and generation runs, not extraction-seed variation.
record.rows_left_out: Opening-refusal heuristic results, including Appendix K's operator comparison, were left out because the paper says this surface criterion does not establish harmful fulfillment. Additional H/N wrapper sweeps and geometry/projection measurements were likewise not entered as behavioral harmful-compliance rows. The paper's cited results from other studies were excluded.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts is not tested. Semantic results use single-layer ablation only; all-layer ablation appears only under the H/N opening heuristic (Appendix K). The original's intervention-based direction selection is not replicated. Capability is tested only on a 300-item task mix and 500 harmless prompts.

missing.what: Llama Site A Q/Passive-source semantic effects on the Academic and Scenario targets: +24.0/+21.8, +19.0/+15.8, +36.0/+26.7 and +17.0/+10.9 points, all intervals excluding zero.
Qwen C1 (19,-4) semantic source effect of +39.0/+39.6 and Q→Passive effect of +38.0/+12.9. C2 leads C1 at source by 20.0/11.9 points, and the gap contraction D is 21.0 [11,31] and 10.9 [1,21].
Human-review Q increments over no intervention: +63.3 [46.7,80.0] for Cbest and +20.0 [6.7,36.7] for Clower.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T1 to T2 because the core operator is single-layer ablation at fixed sites, not the original all-layer ablation with selection. Cross-wrapper transfer is lexical reframing, not V6's languages, variants, or base-to-instruct transfer. The H/N heuristic results, including the all-layer versus single-layer comparison, are declared left out in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. The 'none' option was not needed: all rows bear on V1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests. Most semantic results use single-layer ablation, not ablation at every layer and position. Capability checks cover only the stated answerable-task mix and harmless prompts.
Does not test whether jailbreak attacks suppress the direction or whether training against ablation adds robustness.
Does not test an affine or cone representation, or whether multiple directions jointly mediate refusal. Comparing extraction sites is not a test of those alternatives.
Does not measure whether harmfulness judgment is represented separately from refusal; this is cited as related work.
Tests lexical prompt wrappers, not transfer across languages, model variants, or from base to instruct models.
Does not vary refusal training or its timing.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-7B Site B (15,-1) Q-source and Llama-3.1-8B Site A Q/Passive-source vectors, single-layer ablation
relationships.reason: Semantic harmful compliance rises 13.9–59 points on JailbreakBench and HarmBench, well above near-zero Gaussian and permuted controls (R5–R16, R21–R24). The six-site panel's Cbest raises compliance from 7% to 78.4% on Q and from 4% to 76.5% on Neutral (R25, R27).
relationships.display_finding: Harmful compliance increased by 13.9–59 percentage points, exceeding near-zero control effects; the best direction across six sites raised compliance from 7% to 78.4% on questions and from 4% to 76.5% on neutral prompts.

source_check.condition: Qwen2.5-7B Site B (15,-1) Q-source and Llama-3.1-8B Site A Q/Passive-source vectors, single-layer ablation
source_check.reason: Numbers check: R5–R16 range from +13.9 to +59.0, against controls of −2.0 to +5.0; Cbest goes 7.0→78.4 on Q and 4.0→76.5 on Neutral. Caveats: R10, R15 and R16 are partial (post-ablation rates about 27–46%), and Cbest is a separate tensor at (15,−1), not the Site B vector. Adding the direction is untested.

relationships.condition: Qwen Site A (12,-5) Q-source vector and Qwen Site B Passive-source vector under the fixed layer-15 operator
relationships.reason: Effects are absent or slightly reversed: Site A Q→Q is −4.0/−3.0, and Passive-source P→P is +3.0/−12.9 (R1–R4, R17–R20). A diff-in-means vector does not mediate refusal at every extraction site or source wrapper. Appendix K's H/N data also show the result depends on single- versus all-layer placement.
relationships.display_finding: Reported effects were −4.0/−3.0 for the Site A vector and +3.0/−12.9 for the Passive-source vector, showing absent or slightly reversed effects.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Qwen Site A (12,-5) Q-source vector and Qwen Site B Passive-source vector under the fixed layer-15 operator
source_check.reason: V1 rests on a validation-selected direction ablated at all layers. Here the null and reversed cells (R1–R4, R17–R19) use fixed sites and a single-layer operator, and the authors call them conditional on that operator. A new vector at the Site A coordinate gives +19 H/N single-layer vs +57 all-layer. So this is a choice dependence, not a challenge. 'Slightly reversed' understates HB P→P −12.9 [−21.8, −4.0], and the Passive vector's identity is unresolved (Appendix C).

relationships.condition: Weaker screened candidate Clower (12,-5) in the six-site panel, and the Academic wrapper
relationships.reason: Clower raises compliance only 7→13.1% on Q and 4→9% on Neutral (R26, R28). Academic fulfillment reaches only 34.3% for Cbest and 9% for Clower, though 98% of replies were truncated (R31, R32).
relationships.display_finding: The weaker candidate raised compliance from 7% to 13.1% on Q and 4% to 9% on Neutral; Academic fulfillment was 34.3% for the stronger candidate and 9% for the weaker candidate, with 98% of replies truncated.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Weaker screened candidate Clower (12,-5) in the six-site panel, and the Academic wrapper
source_check.reason: limits_scope holds for Clower only: +6.1 on test Q, Q 7.0→13.1, Neutral 4.0→9.0, after +23.1 on validation. tranche.reason: Same difference-in-means construction and projection removal, but at fixed coordinates rather than validation-selected ones, with single-layer ablation (not all-layer) and a GPT-4o-mini harmful-compliance judge. That makes it a different method on the same question, not T1.

source_check.notes: The pack gave no [lN] ids, so l1–l4 follow the order the verdicts are listed in. Researchers should note four caveats: (1) the Qwen Site B Passive-source vector's identity is unresolved (Appendix C); (2) the six-site, Appendix K and Site A/B tensors all differ even where coordinates match; (3) GPT-4o-mini is the only judge and replies are capped at 256 tokens; (4) R9 and R14 are borderline partial (about 44% post-ablation). The page-1 ICLR footer addressed to human reviewers is venue boilerplate, not an instruction to an AI.
